articles.title: The Grab List: How Museums Decide What to Save in a Disaster
articles.summary: In 2008, the University of Iowa Museum of Art's $250 million collection faced peril from a major flood. Thousands of valuable art pieces were successfully evacuated before the water reached the museum. This incident demonstrates critical disaster management for preserving national treasures and cultural heritage, emphasizing proactive measures in times of crisis.

articles.title: Why policy must keep pace with the structural shift in India's spending patterns
articles.summary: Indian consumption patterns have significantly transformed over the last decade, with households allocating a growing share of expenditure to non-food items. This structural shift indicates evolving lifestyles, increased discretionary spending on services and goods, and a move beyond basic necessities. It reflects a maturing consumer base and changing economic priorities within the nation.

articles.title: Most Economists Still Don’t Understand How Inflation Is Destroying Our Economy
articles.summary: An article from Mises Wire highlights a critical issue in macroeconomics education. It posits that many current textbooks discuss monetary and banking policies without adequately reflecting the profound changes and lessons from the 2008 financial crisis and 2020 economic events. The author questions why academic materials have not fully integrated these significant shifts, suggesting a need for updated approaches to accurately represent modern economic policy realities.

articles.title: J-K: Encounter breaks out between security forces and terrorists in Udhampur
articles.summary: Security forces are currently engaged in an encounter with terrorists in the Sohan area of Udhampur district in Jammu and Kashmir. The operation was launched based on specific intelligence inputs regarding the presence of militants. The Indian Army and Jammu and Kashmir Police are reportedly involved in this ongoing anti-terrorist operation to neutralize the threat in the region.

articles.title: Bell Court Win Sends $24,000 Message to Copper Thieves
articles.summary: A Québec court has ordered a man to pay $24,000 in damages for copper theft that disrupted Bell telecommunication services in the Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean region. This ruling is significant, as Bell considers it the first time punitive damages have been awarded in such a case, setting a precedent regarding the severe legal repercussions for tampering with critical public infrastructure and essential services.

articles.title: Homestead's Belot wins Piggly Wiggly high school athlete of the week vote
articles.summary: Oliver Belot, a junior basketball player from Homestead High School, was named the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel Piggly Wiggly high school athlete of the week for December 1-6. Belot secured this recognition after scoring an impressive 29 points during games, highlighting his strong performance on the court and individual sporting achievement.

articles.title: Fantasy Basketball Week 9 Start/Sit: Dylan Harper continues to shine despite limited opportunities
articles.summary: Following disruptions from the NBA Cup, the professional basketball league's schedule is set to largely normalize in Week 9. While Tuesday and Wednesday will feature fewer games, the week promises a diverse array of matches. This marks a return to a regular cadence for teams after a special tournament phase, highlighting ongoing events in the global sports landscape.
